research_question: Can a useful failure-risk model be trained from appropriate operational data, calibrated, serialized with provenance, loaded by the canonical runtime, and evaluated without leakage?

data_policy.required: real operational data with decision-time features, explicit labels, independent-unit identity, temporal or group split, and sufficient train/validation/evaluation coverage
data_policy.reason: The repository checkout contains adapters and frozen audit/protocol documentation but no data/raw, data/processed, or data/audit files. No model is trained or artifact generated from simulated or historical result data.

prediction_task.definition: Given decision-time observations at time t, predict whether an observed workload failure will occur within a dataset-supported horizon H.
prediction_task.observation_window: Dataset-specific and must be declared before feature extraction.
prediction_task.prediction_horizon: Not instantiated because the required operational data files are absent.
prediction_task.positive_event: Dataset-defined failure occurring after the observation cutoff and within H.
prediction_task.negative_event: An eligible non-failure observation with a complete outcome window.
prediction_task.censoring: Right-censored records must be excluded or explicitly modeled; they may not be labeled negative.
prediction_task.feature_availability_time: At or before the observation cutoff.
prediction_task.label_availability_time: After the prediction horizon; labels are never decision-time features.

split_protocol.primary_rule: Use the frozen dataset-specific split when available; otherwise stop rather than invent a split.
required_controls: incident/entity disjointness where repeated events exist
no evaluation data in threshold tuning or calibration
split_protocol.leakage_stop_condition: If future telemetry, future labels, evaluation groups, evaluation incidents, or evaluation-derived calibration/threshold choices cannot be ruled out, do not train.

baselines.name: existing_runtime_reliability
baselines.purpose: canonical runtime assessor when an artifact is available

model.complexity_policy: No advanced model is permitted before simple baselines establish signal.

calibration.final_evaluation_usage: descriptive only; never used for choosing calibration method or parameters

abstention.goal: test whether abstention changes failure exposure among accepted cases, not merely accuracy

artifact.reload_test: save -> reload -> same input -> same output

reproducibility.scientific_identifier_rule: Use SHA-256 or explicit stable identifiers; never Python hash().

runtime_integration: replay source -> canonical observation -> detector -> reliability artifact -> abstention -> memory -> diagnosis -> recovery -> safety -> validation -> experience
claim_boundary: Results are valid only for the evaluated dataset/protocol; simulator or replay evidence is not production evidence.
